when: Building a badge reprint or pickup list from a seat-edit export where each row is an update to a seat. Trigger when the export has seat, edit, sleeve, account, and badge-name columns, or when a desk asks for pickup badges from an edit log. Also applies when the order account column could be mistaken for a name source.
found: Print one badge per seat, using only the latest edit for that seat (highest edit number). Include the seat only if that latest row's sleeve is yellow (pickup). Skip seats whose latest sleeve is green (already delivered), even if an earlier edit was yellow. Take the badge text only from the badge-name column, never from the order-account column. A blank badge name on a yellow row becomes "Hello, friend". Do not dedupe by account, since one account can cover several seats. Today's sleeve meanings come from the current desk brief and can change.
how: Compared the original export and the accepted sheet row by row. Grouped rows by seat and ordered by edit number. Checked which seats the accepted sheet included and why. The naive method (keep every yellow row, or print the account column) would have produced wrong badges, which matches yesterday's failure.
evidence: Export had 6 rows across 5 seats. One seat had two edits: edit 1 yellow, then edit 2 green. Latest-edit rule excludes it. Using the naive keep-all-yellow rule would have added that seat, so the accepted sheet's 3 badges confirm the rule. One yellow row had a blank name and matched the "Hello, friend" rule. One seat had a green latest row and was correctly excluded. The account column was never used as a badge source, which was the yesterday mistake. Result: accepted sheet matches the method exactly (3 badges, including 1 blank-name fallback).
reconsider: Reconsider if the current desk brief changes sleeve meanings (for example, yellow no longer means pickup), if edit numbers are not monotonic or reset between sessions, or if the export has a timestamp column that should override edit number. Also reconsider if a green-latest seat still needs a reprint because the delivered badge was wrong.
